The driver's explanation is that the extra distance is the co-rider pickup on a platform-matched pooled itinerary. POL-RD-12 excludes distance attributable to collecting or setting down a co-rider on a matched pooled itinerary from excess before POL-RD-01 is applied, and the trip record confirms the matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider as the optimal-route source.

The rider's own profile does not trigger the corroboration requirement of POL-RD-08: deviation_claims_60d is 1, well below the threshold of 4, so no additional corroboration beyond the trace is demanded — and none is needed, because the trace itself shows no qualifying excess.

The driver's profile is context only here: no MATERIAL deviation is recorded under POL-RD-01 (excess 0.96 km, 6.00%), so the POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern check is not engaged and no conduct referral arises from this trip.

The rider's claim that the driver 'picked up someone else' is not a deviation at all on this product. The trip record shows vehicle_type RYDE_POOL and the routing engine matched a pooled itinerary with one co-rider at booking time. A pooled trip is longer than any single rider's solo optimal by construction, which is precisely why POL-RD-12 sets the matched-itinerary figure as the baseline. The rider's $1.50 contested amount is the difference between the solo and pooled optimals, and the policy does not refund it.

ruling.explanation:
Both sides agree on the measurement, and the measurement decides this case. This was a RYDE_POOL shared trip: trip_record.vehicle_type is RYDE_POOL and optimal_route_source records a matched pooled itinerary with one co-rider. Under POL-RD-12 the baseline for the route-deviation test is the matched-itinerary optimal of 16.0 km (trip_record.optimal_distance_km), not the solo-rider figure of 11.5 km (trip_record.solo_optimal_distance_km), which is carried for reference only. The rider's claim measured the trip against the 11.5 km solo route and so cited the wrong field. The distance actually driven is the GPS trace figure of 16.96 km (EV-GPS-02836), which governs over the rounded trip-record copy of 17.0 km under POL-RD-01. Against the 16.0 km baseline the excess is 0.96 km, or 6.00% of optimal. POL-RD-01 establishes a deviation only where the excess is BOTH greater than 20% of optimal AND greater than 0.8 km. The percentage test fails at 6.00%, so no deviation is established, and the co-rider distance is in any event no deviation under POL-RD-12. The trace is clean for policy purposes (133 fixes at 10 s, 100.0% coverage, no gaps, maximum gap 0.0 s), so POL-RD-07(a)-(c) are not met, no independent corroboration is required and there is no POL-RD-10(3) escalation; trip identifiers and timestamps agree across the trip record, trace and fare ledger. There is no billing-integrity defect to correct under POL-RD-09(4): no ERP gantries were charged (tolls_erp 0.0), no airport surcharge was applied, and the charged total of $23.51 reconciles exactly to $12.75 distance (17.0 km x $0.75) + $6.16 time (22.0 min x $0.28) + $3.80 base fare + $0.80 platform fee, so the fare breakdown's charge stands. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-02836-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT); it carries no fact and changes nothing here, because the outcome is decided at the POL-RD-01 threshold and no party relied on an external traffic cause, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and POL-RD-13 leaves the absent advisory as a gap in the bundle rather than a contradiction. The driver-profile check under POL-RD-06 is not engaged (no material deviation on this trip), so no driver-conduct referral arises, and the rider's profile does not trigger additional corroboration under POL-RD-08. Outcome: the rider's claim that the pooled trip was a chargeable deviation is not supported; the charged fare of $23.51 stands and the $1.50 contested is not refunded.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
